title: Batch Config Meridian: continuous workload-driven batching recommender and safe-apply workflow
creator: Aaron Chen
description:
Goal: Implement a continuous 'Meridian' recommender that profiles per-customer and per-model workload signatures and emits safe batching+cache parameter suggestions which can be applied via a staged rollout with automatic rollback triggers. The recommender must be conservative by default and expose explainability (why a suggestion was made) to the Console.

Scope: workload sampling & fingerprinting, heuristic scoring, simulated impact estimation (latency/cost/kv-hit projections), shadow/apply pipeline (shadow replay -> canary -> ramp -> full), rollback criteria, and Console integration for manual review and one-click apply.

Deliverables:
- Workload profiler service (streaming job that computes per-tenant/model distributions: sequence length, request inter-arrival, prefix cache hit probability, token-level autocorrelation).
- Heuristic scoring engine with rules: latency budget adherence, KV cache hit delta threshold, burst safety multiplier, min-viable batch size, and max-latency amplification factor.
- Simulation harness to run proposed batch/cache configs against sampled traces producing projected delta in per-token cost and p95 latency.
- Safe-apply orchestration: shadow replay, 1% canary, 10% ramp with throttled concurrency, continuous monitoring for regressions, and auto-rollback.
- Console UI wireframe & API endpoints for viewing suggestions, audit logs, and manual override.

Non-goals: changing runtime kernel selection heuristics (separate runtime team), modifying model quantization settings.

Success metrics:
- Mean accepted suggestions reduce per-token cost by >=6% on pilot tenants over 30 days.
- No auto-rollback triggers during pilot in >=95% of applies.
- 100% explainability for each suggestion (rule list + sample trace).

acceptance_criteria: Recommender produces suggestions with an explainable rule set and projected cost/latency deltas for each suggestion.
Simulation harness can replay a stored sample trace and return p50/p95/p99 latency and token cost estimates for baseline vs suggested config.
Safe-apply workflow performs: shadow replay -> canary (configurable percent) -> ramp with stabilization windows -> full apply, and emits audit logs at each step.

Automatic rollback triggers when any of: p95 latency increase > 10% absolute, error rate increase > 0.5% absolute, or cost per-token increases by > 3% compared to baseline. Triggers documented and configurable per-tenant.
Console surfaces suggestions with sample traces, risk score, and one-click apply (requires 2 approvers for tenants tagged 'high-impact').
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Over-aggressive batch suggestions could increase tail latency during bursts. Mitigation: conservative burst-safety multiplier and mandatory shadow replay before any canary.
Risk: False positive rollback due to noisy telemetry. Mitigation: smoothing windows and require sustained regression for at least 2 consecutive monitoring buckets (default 60s buckets).
Risk: Incomplete telemetry shapes leading to bad sims. Mitigation: require minimum trace size and fallback to conservative defaults; flag tenants with insufficient telemetry in Console.
Risk: Cross-tenant interference on Dedicated pools. Mitigation: add routing tag checks and disallow auto-apply for tenants on shared Dedicated pools until approved by SRE.
notes: Telemetry surfaces needed: per-tenant sequence length histogram, cache hit by prefix length, inter-arrival distribution, kernel-fill estimate from runtime, per-route latency percentiles, token counts, and error rates.
Consider adding an offline ML model in later phase to predict when batching suggestions will produce stable cost wins (phase 2).
Coordinate rollout with runtime-ops to expose an API for 'estimated kernel fill' and 'max safe batch size' per instance type.
Follow-ups: add end-to-end integration test that runs simulation -> shadow -> canary in CI using small synthetic traces.
